batchName: Late Republic: Marius and the Northern Invaders (121-100 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Late Republic: Marius and the Northern Invaders (121-100 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: Marius was a novus homo. What did that mean?
options: The first of his family to reach high office
A newcomer to Rome from Africa
questions.explanation: The old aristocracy never let him forget it.
questions.sourceQuote: In Rome, though, Marius was a "new man" (*novus homo*), the first of his family to reach high office

questions.question: In 104 BC Jugurtha was paraded in Marius’s triumphus. What was it?
options: The grand victory procession through Rome
A public trial in the Forum
questions.explanation: Jugurtha later died in an underground prison.
questions.sourceQuote: In 104 BC Jugurtha was paraded in Marius's triumph (*triumphus*), the grand victory procession through Rome

questions.question: What was the terror cimbricus?
options: The panic in Rome after the disaster at Arausio
A Roman law against the Cimbri
The name of the Cimbri’s king
questions.explanation: Romans expected the barbarians at the gates at any moment.
questions.sourceQuote: Romans spoke of the "Cimbrian terror" (*terror cimbricus*)

questions.question: Marius was charged with ambitus after an election. What was it?
questions.explanation: He was acquitted, and later a governorship in Spain made him rich.
questions.sourceQuote: He was then charged with electoral bribery (*ambitus*), though he was acquitted.

questions.question: Who were the capite censi that Marius recruited in 107 BC?
options: Men with no property at all, the “head count”
questions.explanation: Normally only men who owned property could serve in the legions.
questions.sourceQuote: men with no property at all, the so-called "head count" (*capite censi*)

questions.question: Which body gave the war against Jugurtha to Marius, overruling the Senate?
options: The Assembly of the plebs (concilium plebis)
questions.explanation: Historians see this as a turning point: generals after Marius copied it.
questions.sourceQuote: took the question to the Assembly of the plebs (*concilium plebis*), the popular voting body.

questions.question: In the old picture of the “Marian reforms”, Marius made soldiers of the proletarii. Who were they?
questions.explanation: Most specialists now call this picture “a construct of modern scholarship”.

questions.question: What was new about the senatus consultum ultimum of 100 BC?
options: For the first time it targeted serving officials
It was the first time the Senate met
It gave Marius a seventh consulship
questions.explanation: It told the magistrates to do whatever was needed to restore order.
questions.sourceQuote: For the first time, such a decree targeted serving officials rather than private citizens.
